02-01.t: Birth of Holter Monitor Inventor Norman Jefferis Holter
02-01.s: American biophysicist Norman Jefferis Holter was born; in 1947 he invented the portable Holter monitor for continuous ambulatory electrocardiography.

02-01.t: Birth of Dr. Sambhu Nath De, Discoverer of Cholera Toxin
02-01.s: Indian medical scientist and pathologist Sambhu Nath De was born in Garibati, Bengal. Using ligated rabbit ileal loops, he discovered the cholera enterotoxin in 1959, transforming global understanding of cholera pathogenesis and secretory diarrhea.

02-02.s: Madras Medical College (MMC) was founded in Chennai, attached to the Government General Hospital. Alongside Calcutta Medical College, it is one of the oldest modern medical institutions in India.

02-02.t: Robert Koch Reports Discovery of the Cholera Bacillus from Calcutta
02-02.s: Working in Calcutta (Kolkata), German microbiologist Robert Koch reported his reasoned conviction on the identification of the comma-shaped cholera bacillus (Vibrio cholerae) as the causative agent of cholera.

02-02.t: India's First Successful Kidney Transplant at CMC Vellore
02-02.s: Dr. A. Mohan Rao and Dr. K. V. Johny performed India's first successful living-donor kidney transplant at Christian Medical College (CMC), Vellore, ushering in the era of organ transplantation in India.

02-03.t: Birth of Pioneer Physician Elizabeth Blackwell
02-03.s: English-born physician Elizabeth Blackwell was born; she became the first woman to graduate from a medical school in the United States and a champion for women's medical education.

02-03.t: First Recorded Pylorotomy for Infantile Pyloric Stenosis
02-03.s: Scottish surgeon Sir Harold Stiles performed the first recorded pylorotomy for hypertrophic pyloric stenosis at the Royal Hospital for Sick Children in Edinburgh.

02-04.s: French obstetrician Adolphe Pinard was born; he invented the Pinard fetal stethoscope (Pinard horn) in 1895 and advanced prenatal obstetric palpation.

02-04.t: World Cancer Day Established in Paris
02-04.s: World Cancer Day was established at the World Summit Against Cancer for the New Millennium in Paris to unite global efforts in cancer prevention, detection, and treatment.

02-05.t: Birth of Anatomist Sir Arthur Keith
02-05.s: Scottish anatomist Sir Arthur Keith was born; together with Martin Flack, he discovered the sinoatrial (Keith-Flack) node in 1907, explaining the heart's natural pacemaker.

02-05.t: First Hospital Application of Caudal Epidural Anesthesia
02-05.s: French urologist Fernand Léon Cathelin first applied caudal sacral epidural access in hospital practice, injecting dilute cocaine for surgical analgesia including hernia repair.

02-06.t: First Successful Use of Charcoal as a Poison Antidote in Humans
02-06.s: French physician Charles Alexandre Hippolyte Amable Bertrand demonstrated that charcoal could successfully treat acute poisoning in humans by testing it on himself.

02-07.s: Japanese pediatrician Tomisaku Kawasaki was born; he first described the childhood mucocutaneous lymph node vasculitis now known as Kawasaki disease.

02-08.t: Birth of Otolaryngologist John McNaughton Epley
02-08.s: American otolaryngologist John McNaughton Epley was born; he developed the Epley canalith repositioning maneuver in 1980 to treat benign paroxysmal positional vertigo.

02-09.t: Birth of Pathologist Howard Taylor Ricketts
02-09.s: American pathologist Howard Taylor Ricketts was born; he discovered the causative bacteria of Rocky Mountain spotted fever and epidemic typhus, giving his name to the genus Rickettsia.

02-09.t: Birth of Nobel Laureate Jacques Monod
02-09.s: French biochemist Jacques Monod was born; he shared the 1965 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discoveries concerning genetic control of enzyme and virus synthesis.

02-10.s: India's Ministry of Health and Family Welfare launched National Deworming Day to combat soil-transmitted helminth infections among children and adolescents aged 1-19 years using albendazole, growing into the world's largest single-day public health deworming program.

02-11.t: BBC Airs First Live Televised Surgery Series
02-11.s: The BBC broadcast the first episode of 'Your Life in Their Hands,' presented by physician Charles Fletcher, televising live hospital operations to demystify modern surgery for the public.

02-13.t: Macintosh Curved Laryngoscope Described in The Lancet
02-13.s: Sir Robert Reynolds Macintosh published the description of his curved laryngoscope blade in The Lancet, formalizing placement of the blade tip in the vallecula for endotracheal intubation.

02-14.t: Great Ormond Street Hospital Opens in London
02-14.s: Founded by Dr. Charles West with 10 beds, Great Ormond Street Hospital opened as the first hospital in the United Kingdom dedicated to inpatient care for children.

02-14.t: Edward Shenton Describes Shenton's Line of the Hip
02-14.s: Guy's Hospital radiographer Edward W. H. Shenton presented a diagnostic radiographic arc of the hip joint, now known as Shenton's line, to the British Electrotherapeutic Society.

02-15.s: At age 22, physician George Huntington presented his classic paper 'On Chorea' in Middleport, Ohio, providing the definitive clinical description of Huntington's disease.
Pennsylvania surgeon Evan O'Neill Kane performed an appendectomy on himself under local anesthesia at Kane Summit Hospital to demonstrate the viability of local anesthesia.

02-15.t: India Certified Free of Guinea Worm Disease
02-15.s: At its February 2000 meeting, the International Commission for the Certification of Dracunculiasis Eradication (ICCDE) reviewed the International Certification Team's report on India, leading to WHO certifying India as free of Guinea worm disease following zero reported cases since 1996.

02-16.s: Cardiothoracic surgeon Prafulla Kumar Sen and his surgical team performed India's first human heart transplant, making it the sixth such procedure worldwide.

02-17.t: Birth of Stethoscope Inventor René Laennec
02-17.s: French physician René-Théophile-Hyacinthe Laennec was born; he invented the stethoscope in 1816 and coined the medical terms cirrhosis and melanoma.

02-17.t: International Committee of the Red Cross Founded
02-17.s: The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) was founded in Geneva to improve battlefield medical care and establish international humanitarian protections for the wounded.

02-17.t: Inauguration of Lady Hardinge Medical College, New Delhi
02-17.s: Lady Hardinge Medical College (LHMC), one of India's earliest and premier medical colleges dedicated to women's medical education, was formally inaugurated in New Delhi by Lord Hardinge.

02-17.t: Inauguration of the Central Drug Research Institute (CDRI), Lucknow
02-17.s: Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru formally inaugurated the Central Drug Research Institute (CDRI) in Lucknow as one of post-independence India's first CSIR national laboratories dedicated to biomedical and pharmaceutical research.

02-18.s: Austrian pediatrician Hans Asperger was born; he described a distinct pattern of neurodevelopmental traits later termed Asperger syndrome.

02-18.t: AIIMS Bill Introduced in Lok Sabha by Rajkumari Amrit Kaur
02-18.s: Union Health Minister Rajkumari Amrit Kaur introduced the bill in the Lok Sabha that became the All India Institute of Medical Sciences Act, 1956, establishing AIIMS New Delhi as an autonomous institute of national importance for medical education and research.

02-19.t: Birth of Ophthalmologist Herman Snellen Sr.
02-19.s: Dutch ophthalmologist Herman Snellen Sr. was born; in 1862 he introduced the Snellen eye chart and optotypes for standardized visual acuity testing.

02-20.t: University of California Establishes Medical Department (Future UCSF)
02-20.s: The Regents of the University of California assumed control of Toland Medical College to form the UC Medical Department, later UCSF, and resolved to admit women students.
Turkish dermatologist Hulusi Behçet was born; in 1937 he described the multisystem inflammatory vasculitis now known as Behçet's disease.

02-21.t: Birth of Vitamin K Discoverer Henrik Dam
02-21.s: Danish biochemist Henrik Dam was born; he won the 1943 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discovering vitamin K and its essential role in blood coagulation.

02-22.t: Birth of Nobel Laureate Virologist Renato Dulbecco
02-22.s: Italian-born American virologist Renato Dulbecco was born; he shared the 1975 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discoveries on how tumor viruses interact with cellular DNA.

02-22.t: Cloning of Dolly the Sheep Announced
02-22.s: Scientists at the Roslin Institute in Scotland announced the successful cloning of Dolly the sheep from an adult somatic cell, transforming genetics and stem cell research.

02-23.t: Birth of CT Scan Co-Inventor Allan MacLeod Cormack
02-23.s: South African-American physicist Allan MacLeod Cormack was born; he shared the 1979 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for developing X-ray computed tomography (CT) scanning.

02-24.t: Establishment of the Calcutta School of Tropical Medicine
02-24.s: Founded by Sir Leonard Rogers of the Indian Medical Service, the Calcutta School of Tropical Medicine (CSTM) was established in Kolkata as a dedicated postgraduate research institute for tropical diseases.

02-24.t: Birth of Tumor Angiogenesis Pioneer Judah Folkman
02-24.s: American medical scientist Judah Folkman was born; he founded the field of tumor angiogenesis research, showing how tumors recruit blood vessels and inspiring anti-angiogenic cancer therapies.

02-24.t: Employees' State Insurance (ESI) Scheme First Implemented
02-24.s: Administered by the Employees' State Insurance Corporation (ESIC) under the ESI Act of 1948, India's social health insurance scheme for workers was first put into effect in Kanpur and Delhi.

02-25.t: Birth of Anatomical Pathology Founder Giovanni Battista Morgagni
02-25.s: Italian physician Giovanni Battista Morgagni was born; his 1761 work correlated postmortem findings with clinical symptoms, establishing modern anatomical pathology.

02-26.s: The first televised kidney transplant was broadcast on television's Today Show, bringing organ transplantation surgery into public view.

02-27.t: Birth of Insulin Co-Discoverer Charles Best
02-27.s: Canadian medical scientist Charles Herbert Best was born; as Frederick Banting's research assistant in 1921, he played a central role in isolating insulin for diabetes treatment.

02-28.t: Birth of Cortisone Co-Discoverer Philip Showalter Hench
02-28.s: American physician Philip Showalter Hench was born; he shared the 1950 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discovering cortisone and its therapeutic effect in rheumatoid arthritis.

02-28.t: Birth of Transplant Immunology Pioneer Peter Medawar
02-28.s: British biologist Peter Medawar was born; his work on acquired immune tolerance and transplant rejection earned him the 1960 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.

02-28.t: Commissioning of Tata Memorial Hospital, Mumbai
02-28.s: The Sir Dorabji Tata Trust commissioned Tata Memorial Hospital (TMH) in Parel, Mumbai, which grew into India's oldest and largest comprehensive cancer treatment and research center.

02-28.t: Release of Indigenous CSIR-CDRI Drugs and Leishmaniasis Diagnostic Kit
02-28.s: Prime Minister P. V. Narasimha Rao released new drugs developed by CSIR-CDRI (BESEB and Chandonium iodide) along with a diagnostic kit for leishmaniasis and new drug technologies to the nation.

02-29.s: The European Organisation for Rare Diseases (EURORDIS) coordinated the first Rare Disease Day on the rarest calendar date to raise awareness and improve care for rare diseases.
